bullets.text: Israel has confirmed its soldiers fired at a car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza, and has opened a criminal investigation. The child initially survived the attack and pleaded for help, but her body was later recovered along with those of six relatives.
Seven people, including five Americans, died in a safari helicopter crash in Kenya. Among the victims were an intelligence chief from Ecuador and a Telemundo executive.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the deadliest in the country's history, with official data reporting at least 2,325 deaths from the virus.
Internal Northern Territory Police data reveals a surge in the number of children and teenagers being held in police station cells under the CLP government.
A police task force has been launched to investigate sexual abuse complaints around Byron Bay's music scene from the early 2000s, following an ABC investigation.
Australia's government debt is projected to briefly reach a record $1 trillion today.

The US government debt has reached $40 trillion, indicating a historic rate of borrowing, while the Treasury plans to increase long-term bond purchases to stabilize the market amidst rising borrowing costs.
Federal Reserve officials have expressed growing concern over persistent inflation, with many policymakers ready to increase borrowing costs further.
Moderna's shares doubled after its skin cancer vaccine, developed with Merck, showed positive results in a late-stage trial, leading to significant gains and impacting short sellers.
